review_perspective: Independent accessibility review of exact requirement 185; source, existing R4 assertion/report inspection and two rendered artifact observations; no new browser execution or ledger edit.
verdict: Supports the bounded requirement-185 shared historical-import interaction and context criteria at the bound current source. Does not certify overall accessibility, other 61 sign-offs, full application roles or programme completion.

requirements.pass_condition: Past-duty upload, preview, correction, review and apply use the shared import interaction patterns.
support: past-duties.ts render calls the actual ui.ts steps helper with Select workbook, Set up, Review, Apply. operational-import.ts uses the same helper for its distinct CSV workflow.

ui.ts steps renders an ol with accessible name Progress; li current uses aria-current=step, decorative dots are aria-hidden, completed items include visually-hidden (done). Step labels remain readable text; these informational steps are not misleading interactive tabs.

R4 recovery progress() asserts all four data-state values and exactly one aria-current before completion, none when all four are done. Native focused Enter activates initial retry, template/rejection downloads, inspect, preview, apply and saved-detail recovery.

Held Apply asserts native disabled state at stage 3 and pressing Enter again produces one mutation. Confirmed response sets stage 4; saved readback failure and repeated GET-only recovery retain completion. Unknown Apply remains review stage with explicit fresh-preview message and no repeated mutation.

R4 boundary correction fixture exercises row-details opening, changed duty type, stale preview, blocked Apply, re-preview and explicit warnings/correction confirmation. These retain stage 2 until actual Apply response.
limits: Recovery keyboard helper calls focus() then real page.keyboard.press(Enter); it proves native activation of exercised buttons, not a complete sequential Tab/Space/arrow-key matrix or touch equivalence.
File selection uses Playwright setInputFiles rather than native operating-system picker interaction; selectOption/check cover resulting state, not every native key path.

requirements.pass_condition: Historical-data explanations and date context remain distinct, and existing historical import payloads and outcomes are preserved.
support: Current markup explicitly states selected historical month, returned preview month and worksheet, consequences for statistics/scoring and unchanged existing call levels; review describes corrections, dates, start/end times and local hospital time.

Saved outcome is a separately named Last applied import section with role=status outcome and escaped filename/selected month/returned month/worksheet. It remains explicitly scoped when a same-file re-inspection or different unsaved file starts a new draft. Missing returned context reads Not returned.

Boundary fixtures cover previous December on January 1, leap February, explicit current-month correction, selected/returned-month mismatch with replayed outcome, and missing returned month/worksheet. Assertions compare saved context and require filename as text, never injected historical markup.

R4 recovery and boundaries inspect actual multipart File bytes/options/preview_hash and exact template/rejection download bytes. This is frontend transport preservation under intercepted requests, not backend parsing or persisted-outcome certification.
limits: All API responses are intercepted in an Administrator component fixture. Server authorisation, backend parser, real production permissions and actual database outcomes are outside these tests.

focus_owner_support: retainActionFocus records whether the trigger owned focus, listens for deliberate focus movement, checks connected/current ownership before restoration, and restores only when active focus has fallen to body or remains trigger.

R4 assertions verify repeated failed safe-read retry retains retry focus; blocked unknown-outcome Apply retains Apply focus; superseded initial load and superseded Apply retain outside focus and do not inject stale outcomes.
No new keydown interception or interactive step-rail behavior was introduced by the requirement-185 presentation.
text_resize_support: Visual suite uses real computed font sizes for each current host element and writes doubled sizes; it asserts the chosen step-label computed size doubled exactly, then measures glyph bounding boxes inside round step dots and progress scrollWidth<=clientWidth+1.
12 visual contexts cover Chromium/Firefox/WebKit at 320 and 844 emulated widths in light/dark. Normal preview plus actual doubled-step screenshots are produced for each.

Independent visual observation of Chromium 320 dark doubled-text screenshot: all four labels readable, wrapped in order, no visibly clipped circle glyphs. WebKit 320 light preview screenshot: heading, historical context, setup controls, review information and Apply button readable within the panel; comparison table scrolls locally.
honest_remaining_gaps: No native screen-reader/assistive-technology execution, announcement-order verification or browser accessibility-tree snapshot. Status/alert semantics are inspected in source and used by locators; this does not prove announcement delivery after whole-host replacement.
No physical-device run, operating-system file picker walkthrough, mobile software-keyboard/rotation check or real touch pass; desktop viewport emulation only.
No forced-colors/high-contrast execution in R4 and no measured foreground/background contrast matrix. Light/dark screenshots alone cannot establish WCAG contrast compliance.

Enlarged geometry assertions are specific to progress container and step dots. They do not prove full-panel/body reflow, label clipping across every language, browser zoom equivalence, sticky-shell focus visibility or every field at 200 percent. Two screenshots were visually inspected by this reviewer; all 24 were not independently viewed.

Existing onchange branches replace host.innerHTML after filter/confirmation/setup/row edits without using retainActionFocus. Sequential field focus/caret preservation across those changes is not asserted here. Baseline already contains the filter/confirmation render pattern, so this is an existing accessibility concern, not established as a new 185 regression.

Existing member-import-table comparison wrappers have no explicit tabindex or accessible region name. Native-engine scroll behavior may differ; R4 does not establish keyboard-only horizontal table access. Baseline has the same wrapper; this is a separate existing accessibility task.

The fixture mounts the component inside a minimal main element as Administrator. It does not exercise actual shell navigation, role variations, dialogs, sticky rails, all route headings or permission-based control exposure.

The progress ol itself has no live region. Working/outcome messages use role=status and failures may use role=alert, but step changes being announced intelligibly and without duplication remain native-AT work.

historical_limit: R1 stylesheet timeout, R2 native Chromium crash and R3 template-download timeout remain retained failures with causes unproven. This review does not overwrite them or reaccept older 61 checkpoint sign-offs.
